" <p> Dawkins , whilst occasionally expressing discomfort with the crudeness of the Bush administration , focused his critiques on the religious motivations of political actors rather than the structural imperatives of global capitalism and imperial expansion . By localising the problem of war in the religious beliefs of individual leaders -- Bush 's evangelicalism , Blair 's Catholicism -- Dawkins prevented a systemic critique of the British and American states . The problem , in the New Atheist view , was not the capitalist war machine or the pursuit of global @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ were praying before they pressed the button . <p> This deflection is ideologically consequential . It allowed the New Atheist intellectual to condemn a specific war on the grounds of its leader 's irrationality whilst remaining entirely uncritical of the system that produced both the war and the leader . Dawkins 's critique of Bush 's religion thus functions as a kind of political inoculation : it generates the appearance of principled opposition to the war whilst leaving the underlying structures of imperial power entirely intact . The critique that should be directed at the military-industrial complex , the oil industry , and the architecture of American global hegemony is instead redirected at the personal theological beliefs of individual actors . <p> Robert Wright observed as early as 2009 that the New Atheists were , in terms of foreign policy , consistently right-wing , supporting or failing to oppose the broad contours of American military adventurism whilst reserving their analytical energy for attacks on the religious motivations of individual actors . Trajce Stojanov has more recently argued that New Atheism functions as an ideological tool of neoliberalism , Western hegemony @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ and its compatibility with the " clash of civilisations " frame . Even if one does not accept every element of that thesis , it captures a real tendency : New Atheism consistently presents Western modernity as the default horizon of reason whilst casting non-Western religious societies as backward , dangerous , or unfinished . <p> The Structural Consequences of Civilisational Thinking <p> The consequences of New Atheism 's uncritical relationship with Western militarism extend beyond the specific wars it supported or failed to oppose . By providing a secular , scientifically credentialed justification for the framework of civilisational conflict , the movement contributed to a cultural climate in which extraordinary violence against Muslim-majority populations became intellectually respectable . Sam Harris 's advocacy for racial profiling , nuclear first strikes , and the routine acceptance of civilian casualties as " collateral damage " was not the position of a fringe extremist but of a bestselling author celebrated by mainstream liberal culture . <p> Critics have noted the deeply troubling parallels between this New Atheist discourse and older , discredited forms of " scientific racism . " Just as eighteenth and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ inferiority of colonised peoples to justify slavery and colonialism , New Atheist figures use their status as scientists to make sweeping , denigrating claims about " the Muslim world , " presenting it as a monolith incapable of rationality or civil society . This narrative serves a clear political function : if a billion people are viewed as inherently irrational and hostile , then their subjugation , the bombing of their countries , and the support for oppressive regimes that act against them are not only justified but necessary for the " survival " of the West . <p> New Atheism functions as " an intellectual defense of empire " captures this dynamic precisely . By prioritising atheism over anti-imperialism , the movement aligns with elite liberalism 's instincts : defending " civilisation " whilst remaining blind to its coercive foundations . The result is a philosophy that can dissect ancient superstitions with clinical precision , yet remains completely blind to the corporate , militaristic , and imperial forces that shape the modern world . <p> Structural Contradictions and the Enlightenment Fetish <p> The foundational texts of New Atheism are @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Enlightenment . This perspective treats the Enlightenment as an isolated , immaculate conception of reason that occurred within the geographic boundaries of Western Europe , entirely independent of the rest of the world . Dawkins and Harris present this flawed , Eurocentric version of history as a universal benchmark , casting any society that did not follow Western Europe 's specific historical trajectory as pathologically deficient , culturally backward , and in need of external correction . <p> This view completely ignores the extensive scholarship of postcolonial theorists who have demonstrated that the European Enlightenment was structurally and financially dependent on the violent exploitation of the Americas , the transatlantic slave trade , and the colonisation of Asia and Africa . Enrique Dussel has argued that the very concept of modernity is inseparable from the conquest of the Americas , which provided both the material resources and the theoretical apparatus -- in the form of racial hierarchy -- necessary for the European Enlightenment to take the form it did ( Dussel , p.65-70 ) . Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak similarly demonstrates that the development of modern philosophy and science was intimately @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Spivak , p.1-27 ) . Edward Said 's Orientalism reveals how the categories of Western knowledge production -- including the social sciences that New Atheists claim to represent -- emerged from and served the interests of colonial power ( Said , p.7 ) . <p> By presenting a cleansed , Eurocentric version of this history as universal reason , New Atheists engage in a form of historical mystification that serves contemporary imperial interests . The narrative that Western science and secularism emerged solely from intellectual curiosity , free from the taint of colonial violence , is not merely historically inaccurate ; it is ideologically functional . It allows the inheritors of colonial wealth to present their advantages as the natural rewards of superior rationality rather than the spoils of historical violence . <p> Charles Taylor 's analysis in A Secular Age similarly challenges the linear narrative of secularisation that New Atheism uncritically adopts . Taylor demonstrates that the emergence of Western secular modernity was a complex , contingent , and historically specific process , not the inevitable outcome of rational progress ( Taylor , p.1-22 ) . By treating this @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ New Atheists reproduce the very dogmatism -- the unquestioned certainty about the direction of history -- that they attribute to religious believers . <p> Scientism and the Failure of Epistemology <p> New Atheism 's epistemological arrogance , often termed " scientism , " represents a further dimension of its hollowness . The movement presents a view of rationality that is severely truncated , failing to account for the many ways in which humans derive meaning and value . In its demand that all claims be empirically verifiable , New Atheism echoes the logical positivism of the early twentieth century -- a philosophical doctrine long critiqued and largely abandoned for its own inherent contradictions . Whitley Kaufman notes that New Atheism contributes little of lasting value to serious philosophical debate , preferring caricature , ridicule , and scientistic overreach to actual engagement with theology or philosophy . <p> By insisting that only scientific inquiry can provide " real " knowledge , New Atheists paradoxically exclude the very tools of logic , philosophy , and ethics necessary to build a coherent worldview . This leads to a form of anti-intellectualism where complex @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ either dismissed as delusion or reduced to simplistic biological or evolutionary functions . Terry Eagleton observes in Reason , Faith , and Revolution that Dawkins and Harris are " ill-equipped to grapple with the very subject-matter they seek to denigrate , " lacking the theological and philosophical literacy necessary to engage seriously with the traditions they attack ( Eagleton , p.2 ) . The result is a new dogma of " scientific " certainty that is just as inflexible as the religious dogmatism it attacks . <p> This epistemological narrowness has concrete political consequences . Because the New Atheist framework privileges only empirically verifiable claims , it is structurally incapable of engaging with the moral and political dimensions of historical injustice . Questions of reparation , sovereignty , self-determination , and historical accountability can not be resolved by the methods of evolutionary biology or neuroscience . By restricting the domain of legitimate knowledge to the empirically verifiable , New Atheism excludes precisely the categories of analysis -- historical , political , moral -- necessary to understand and respond to structures of oppression . <p> Scientific Racism and the Return of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ in favour of biological and cultural reductionism , they inevitably reproduce older structures of racial hierarchy . The transition from New Atheism 's critique of religion to a soft form of scientific racism and cultural supremacy was not an accidental detour ; it was an organic development of its core logic . Sam Harris 's defence of Charles Murray -- the co-author of The Bell Curve , a widely discredited text suggesting a genetic basis for racial disparities in IQ -- demonstrates how easily New Atheist rationalism can pivot to justify domestic and global inequalities . <p> By substituting " culture " or " theological susceptibility " for the older pseudoscientific category of " race , " New Atheists resurrect the classic mission civilisatrice for the twenty-first century . The old colonial argument stated that the West had a moral duty to colonise and govern non-white populations because they were racially incapable of self-governance . The New Atheist iteration modifies this slightly : The West has a moral right to dominate , bomb , and police the global South because their religious belief systems render them culturally incapable of rationality @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ identical ; only the vocabulary has changed . <p> Josh Rosenau 's analysis of New Atheism 's trajectory traces how the movement has " slid into the alt-right , " embracing Islamophobia , racism , and a reactionary politics that is anything but enlightened . This is not an aberration but a logical consequence of the movement 's foundational commitments . A framework that essentialises non-Western cultures as irrational and hostile , that provides intellectual cover for military intervention , and that reproduces civilisational hierarchies in secular language is well-adapted to the reactionary political environment of the early twenty-first century . <p> How the Apolitical Becomes Political <p> The most sophisticated dimension of New Atheism 's political function lies in the way it produces consent for existing power structures precisely through its claim to be above politics . By presenting itself as a neutral , scientific , and universal enterprise , it naturalises the assumptions of Western liberal hegemony -- the superiority of Western institutions , the rationality of Western violence , the irrationality of non-Western resistance -- in a form that appears to be the outcome of impartial reason @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Gramsci would recognise as the operation of hegemony : the consent of the governed is secured not through force but through the manufacture of a common sense that presents the interests of the ruling class as universal interests . New Atheism performs this function with particular efficiency because its credentials as a scientific , rational enterprise lend it an authority that explicitly political discourse does not possess . When a scientist with evolutionary credentials declares Islam to be " the greatest force for evil in the world today " , that declaration carries the apparent weight of empirical fact rather than ideological assertion . <p> Saba Mahmood 's analysis of the politics of religious difference in secular liberal states is illuminating here . Mahmood demonstrates that the secular state 's management of religion is not a neutral administrative matter but a deeply political project that shapes the identities and capacities of its subjects ( Mahmood , p.1-20 ) . The New Atheist celebration of Western secularism as the universal endpoint of human development is therefore not merely philosophically naive ; it is complicit in the political project of securing Western @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ outcome of reason and progress . <p> The Limits of the New Atheist Legacy <p> The intellectual and political legacy of New Atheism is now clearly visible in the cultural landscape . The movement 's decline -- fractured by internal culture wars , its own inconsistencies , and the collapse of several of its prominent figures into openly reactionary positions -- illustrates the consequences of a philosophy built on insufficient foundations . The New Atheist who championed reason and evidence found himself , within a decade , defending the scientific respectability of racial IQ research , celebrating anti-Muslim bigotry as " brave , " and aligning with the political right on questions of immigration , free speech , and " Western values . " <p> This trajectory was not a betrayal of the movement 's original commitments but their logical fulfilment . A framework that essentialises non-Western cultures as irrational , that provides intellectual cover for Western military violence , that reproduces civilisational hierarchies , and that refuses to engage with the material conditions of global inequality has nowhere else to go . The critique of religion , unmoored from @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ becomes a vehicle for the very prejudices and power structures it claims to oppose . <p> T.J. Coles 's analysis of how New Atheism " exploited rationalism to promote war " over the two decades since its emergence documents the concrete political consequences of this trajectory with forensic precision . The movement provided a secular , progressive-seeming rationale for policies -- racial profiling , pre-emptive warfare , the suspension of civil liberties for Muslim populations -- that would have been difficult to defend on explicitly political grounds . In doing so , it served the interests of the security state more effectively than any openly partisan political argument could have . <p> What a Genuine Critique of Religion Would Look Like <p> New Atheism 's failures do n't disprove atheism or secularism ; rather , they highlight the need for a more intellectually rigorous and politically honest approach . To truly honour Enlightenment values , a critique of religion must be built on entirely different foundations . <p> First , it would situate religious belief within its material , historical , and political contexts , recognising that religious movements are @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ errors . It would take seriously the sociological and anthropological literature on religion , engaging with the actual diversity of religious practice and belief rather than attacking a straw man of fundamentalist literalism . <p> Second , it would apply its critical standards consistently across all sources of irrationality and violence , including the secular ones . A secularism that condemns religious violence but ignores or excuses state violence is not secularism at all ; it is merely a tribal identity marker for those who wish to feel superior to the targets of Western military power . True scepticism demands that the same rigorous scrutiny applied to religious claims be applied to the claims of governments , military establishments , and economic institutions . <p> Third , it would ground its universalist commitments in a genuine engagement with the universality of human suffering . The test of a claimed commitment to universal human dignity is not how one responds to suffering caused by enemies but how one responds to suffering caused by one 's own state or allies . By this test , New Atheism fails comprehensively . Its indifference @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ caused by Western military action , and its contemptuous dismissal of Muslim victims as complicit in their own destruction reveal that its universalism was always selective -- a universalism of the powerful . <p> Fourth , it would engage seriously with the insights of postcolonial theory , recognising that the history of Western modernity is inseparable from the history of colonial violence . A secularism that celebrates the Enlightenment without reckoning with the slave trade and colonial conquest that financed it is not a secularism of truth but of convenient myth . <p> The Need for Political Atheism <p> What the critique of New Atheism ultimately demands are a politically engaged , historically informed , and materially grounded atheism -- one that understands the critique of religion not as an end in itself but as part of a broader commitment to human emancipation . Such an atheism would recognise that religion can function as both an instrument of oppression and a vehicle of liberation , depending on the social and political context in which it operates . It would direct its analytical energies not only at the theological but at @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , and political arrangements that produce and sustain human suffering . <p> Tariq Ali 's formulation of a " clash of fundamentalisms " -- in which Western secular fundamentalism is as much a threat to human freedom as religious fundamentalism -- captures this spirit ( Ali , p.3 ) . Terry Eagleton 's critique of the " Ditchkins " ( Dawkins and Hitchens combined ) as " secular theologians " who have replaced one form of unquestioned dogma with another ( Eagleton , p.4 ) points in the same direction . Hamid Dabashi 's argument that the opposition between " Islam " and " the West " is a manufactured binary that serves the interests of both Western imperialism and religious authoritarianism offers a more sophisticated framework than anything New Atheism has produced . <p> True intellectual emancipation does not come from lecturing the victims of Western imperialism on their lack of scientific literacy whilst their homes are being destroyed by Western-manufactured bombs . It requires a critique that targets both religious obscurantism and the secular war machines of empire , recognising that the struggle for a rational world is @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ and equitable global order . <p> The Delusion of a Hollow Creed <p> The historical legacy of New Atheism is not one of genuine intellectual liberation or the universal expansion of human freedom . It is , instead , a case study in how the language of secularism and scientific rationalism can be co-opted to serve the interests of state violence , imperial expansion , and civilisational supremacy . By treating religion as an isolated cognitive disease and ignoring the material realities of capitalism , colonialism , and geopolitics , New Atheism constructed a hollow , apolitical framework that systematically protected Western hegemony from meaningful critique . <p> The movement 's profound moral failures -- its callous indifference to the structural violence inflicted upon Palestinians , its intellectual defence of American militarism , its willingness to justify torture and pre-emptive nuclear strikes in the language of rational calculation -- reveal that New Atheism was never truly about the pursuit of truth . It was an ideological project designed to comfort the affluent citizens of the global North , reassuring them that their wealth , security , and global dominance were @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of global exploitation and military violence . <p> Richard Dawkins and Sam Harris offered timely and sometimes accurate critiques of religious literalism and clerical authority . But they faltered catastrophically in addressing the suffering in Palestine , the hypocrisies of Western militarism , and the structural inequalities of the global order . Their movement 's rapid descent from bestselling rationalism to reactionary culture-war politics was not an accident but an inevitability . A philosophy that can not account for empire , that can not see the humanity of the occupied , and that can not direct its scepticism towards the powerful as readily as towards the weak is not a philosophy of liberation . It is a philosophy of comfortable complicity . <p> To counter this legacy , any contemporary critique of religion must be grounded in a materialist , historical , and anti-imperialist framework . It must recognise that religious beliefs can not be separated from the socio-economic conditions in which they are formed and practised . It must apply its moral standards consistently , measuring the violence of states and non-state actors by the same criteria . And @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ not as a secondary consideration , but as the primary test of its commitment to the universal human dignity it claims to uphold . <p> Reason without empathy , and secularism without an unwavering commitment to the equal dignity of all human life , quickly decays into an instrument of tyranny . The gospel of the gilded cage -- the promise of intellectual freedom that serves , in practice , to secure the bars of imperial power -- is ultimately no gospel at all . <h> Subscribe to Our Newsletter <p> V.A .
